library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wilkins_2019_avelumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wilkins_2019_avelumab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12406> (open access, PMC6617853)

Avelumab is a human anti-PD-L1 IgG1 monoclonal antibody. Wilkins 2019
describes its serum pharmacokinetics in 1,827 patients with 14 types of
advanced solid tumors, given 1 to 20 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks. The model is
linear two-compartment with a sigmoid time-varying clearance taken from
the nivolumab model of Liu et al. (Eq. 1):

\[ \mathrm{CL}_{i}(t) = \mathrm{TVCL}_i \cdot
   \exp\!\left(\frac{I_{\max,i}\, t^{\gamma}}{T_{50}^{\gamma} + t^{\gamma}}\right)
   \cdot \exp(\eta_{\mathrm{CL},i}), \qquad
   I_{\max,i} = I_{\max} + \eta_{I_{\max},i} \]

where \(t\) is the time after the first dose in days. The typical
\(I_{\max}\) is zero for 12 of the 14 tumor types and negative (a decrease
in clearance) for metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma (mMCC) and squamous cell
carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN). Its additive random effect lets an
individual's clearance rise or fall over time in every tumor type. Thirteen
covariate effects act on CL and four on the central volume V1, all
normalised to the population medians.

The authors' NONMEM control stream is published as Data S1 of the article.
The packaged model follows its structure (covariate normalisation,
imputation and caps, and the tumor-type switches), with the final
estimates from Table 2.

# Population

Data come from three trials: JAVELIN Solid Tumor (phase I, n = 1,688),
JAVELIN Solid Tumor JPN (phase I in Japan, n = 51) and JAVELIN Merkel 200
(phase II, mMCC, n = 88). Together they give 10,637 serum concentrations
(Table 1). Median baseline age was 63 years (19-91) and median weight
71 kg (30.4-204); 47.8% of patients were female, 76.2% White, 11.3% Asian
and 4.8% Black or African American. Most patients (97.3%) received
10 mg/kg every 2 weeks. The largest tumor groups were NSCLC (18.6%),
gastric / GEJ cancer (15.7%), urothelial carcinoma (13.6%) and ovarian
cancer (12.5%); SCCHN was 8.4% and mMCC 4.8%.

The same information is available programmatically from
`readModelDb("Wilkins_2019_avelumab")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` | log(0.0308 L/h) | Table 2, CL |
| `lvc` | log(3.42 L) | Table 2, central volume |
| `lvp` | log(0.918 L) | Table 2, peripheral volume |
| `lq` | log(0.0313 L/h) | Table 2, intercompartmental CL |
| `cl_time_max` | 0, fixed | Table 2, Imax for all other tumor types |
| `cl_time_max_scchn` | -0.284 | Table 2, Imax SCCHN |
| `cl_time_max_mcc` | -0.387 | Table 2, Imax mMCC |
| `lcl_t50` | log(68.4 day) | Table 2, T50 for all other tumor types (also used for SCCHN in Data S1) |
| `lcl_t50_mcc` | log(131 day) | Table 2, T50 mMCC |
| `lcl_time_hill` | log(2.91) | Table 2, gamma for all other tumor types |
| `lcl_time_hill_scchn` | log(0.73) | Table 2, gamma for SCCHN |
| `lcl_time_hill_mcc` | log(1.68) | Table 2, gamma for mMCC |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.324, 0.362 | Table 2, body weight on CL and V1 |
| `e_sexf_cl`, `e_sexf_vc` | -0.15, -0.160 | Table 2, female sex on CL and V1 |
| `e_age_cl` | -0.12 | Table 2, age on CL |
| `e_race_black_cl` | -0.12 | Table 2, Black race on CL |
| `e_alb_cl`, `e_alb_vc` | -0.438, -0.278 | Table 2, albumin on CL and V1 |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.0579 | Table 2, eGFR on CL |
| `e_tumsz_cl` | 0.0592 | Table 2, tumor burden on CL |
| `e_ada_pos_cl` | 0.123 | Table 2, ever positive for ADA on CL |
| `e_crp_cl` | 0.0677 | Table 2, CRP on CL |
| `e_plt_cl` | 0.0603 | Table 2, platelets on CL |
| `e_ast_cl` | -0.0514 | Table 2, AST on CL |
| `e_no_opioid_cl` | -0.0445 | Table 2, not taking concomitant opioids on CL |
| `e_prior_bio_cl`, `e_prior_bio_vc` | -0.0508, -0.0526 | Table 2, previous use of biologics on CL and V1 |
| `etalcl + etalvc + etalvp` | 0.0535; 0.0171, 0.0332; 0.0633, -0.014, 0.858 | Table 2 IIV rows, placed by the Data S1 `$OMEGA BLOCK(3)` (see Assumptions) |
| `etacl_time_max` | 0.0596 (additive) | Table 2, IIV on Imax |
| `propSd`, `addSd` | 0.162, 2.43 ug/mL | Table 2, residual variability |
| Covariate medians (71 kg, 63 y, 39 g/L, 85.9, 60 mm, 10.7 mg/L, 247, 22 U/L) | -- | Data S1 `$PK`; Table 1 medians |
| Covariate caps and imputation of missing values | -- | Data S1 `$PK` |
| Eq. 1 time-varying CL, Eqs. 2-3 covariate forms | -- | Methods, Data S1 |
| Two-compartment structure, combined residual error | -- | Results, Data S1 (`ADVAN3 TRANS4`, `$ERROR`) |

# Virtual cohort

The individual data are not public. The cohort below has three arms of
150 patients each: urothelial carcinoma (one of the 12 tumor types with no
typical time effect), SCCHN and mMCC. Continuous covariates are drawn from
log-normal or normal distributions centred on the Table 1 medians and kept
inside the Table 1 ranges by redrawing out-of-range values. Binary
covariates use the Table 1 frequencies, with the mMCC female fraction
(26.1%) from the JAVELIN Merkel 200 column.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2019)
n_arm <- 150

draw_in_range <- function(n, draw, lo, hi) {
  x <- draw(n)
  bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  while (any(bad)) {
    x[bad] <- draw(sum(bad))
    bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  }
  x
}

make_arm <- function(arm, id0, scchn, mcc, p_female) {
  n <- n_arm
  data.frame(
    id = id0 + seq_len(n),
    arm = arm,
    WT = draw_in_range(n, function(k) rlnorm(k, log(71), 0.22), 30.4, 204),
    AGE = draw_in_range(n, function(k) rnorm(k, 63, 11), 19, 91),
    ALB = draw_in_range(n, function(k) rnorm(k, 39, 5), 10, 52),
    CRCL = draw_in_range(n, function(k) rlnorm(k, log(85.9), 0.3), 21.8, 398),
    TUMSZ = draw_in_range(n, function(k) rlnorm(k, log(60), 0.7), 10, 750),
    CRP = draw_in_range(n, function(k) rlnorm(k, log(10.7), 1.4), 0.2, 1770),
    PLT = draw_in_range(n, function(k) rlnorm(k, log(247), 0.35), 71, 1130),
    AST = draw_in_range(n, function(k) rlnorm(k, log(22), 0.45), 2, 210),
    SEXF = rbinom(n, 1, p_female),
    RACE_BLACK = rbinom(n, 1, 0.0476),
    ADA_POS = rbinom(n, 1, 0.0416),
    CONMED_OPIOID = rbinom(n, 1, 0.669),
    PRIOR_BIO = rbinom(n, 1, 0.262),
    TUMTP_SCCHN = scchn,
    TUMTP_MCC = mcc
  )
}

cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_arm("Urothelial carcinoma", 0, 0, 0, 0.478),
  make_arm("SCCHN", n_arm, 1, 0, 0.478),
  make_arm("mMCC", 2 * n_arm, 0, 1, 0.261)
)
cohort$arm <- factor(cohort$arm, levels = c("Urothelial carcinoma", "SCCHN", "mMCC"))
```

Every patient receives 10 mg/kg as a 1-hour IV infusion every 2 weeks for
26 weeks (13 doses). Observations are dense over the first and the last
dosing interval and daily in between.

```{r events}
tau <- 336
dose_times <- seq(0, by = tau, length.out = 13)
last_start <- max(dose_times)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 8, 12, seq(24, tau, by = 12),
  seq(tau, last_start, by = 24),
  last_start + c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 8, 12), seq(last_start + 24, last_start + tau, by = 12)
)))

doses <- cohort |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = dose_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = 10 * WT, dur = 1, evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
obs <- cohort |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Wilkins_2019_avelumab")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = events, keep = "arm",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

# Replicate Figure 2a: first dosing cycle at 10 mg/kg

Figure 2a of the paper is a visual predictive check of the first cycle.
There, the observed median is about 230 ug/mL at the end of the infusion
and falls to roughly 25-30 ug/mL by the end of the 2-week interval.

```{r fig2a, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
first_cycle <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= tau) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = stats::median(Cc),
    lo = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    hi = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(first_cycle, aes(time, median)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "orange", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(colour = "navy", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Avelumab concentration (ug/mL)",
    title = "Simulated first cycle, 10 mg/kg (median and 90% interval)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2a of Wilkins 2019 (all tumor types pooled)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Replicate Figure 3: change in clearance over time

```{r fig3, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
cl_rel <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cl_rel = cl / cl_base) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

ggplot(dplyr::filter(cl_rel, id %% 3 == 0), aes(time / 24, cl_rel, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (day)", y = "CL(t) / CL at time zero",
    title = "Individual time course of clearance by tumor type",
    caption = "Replicates the corresponding panels of Figure 3 of Wilkins 2019 (one in three patients drawn)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Replicate Figure 5: clearance at baseline and after 26 weeks

Figure 5 shows a marked fall in clearance by steady state in mMCC
(medians about 0.034 to 0.025 L/h in non-responders and 0.027 to
0.018 L/h in responders). In urothelial carcinoma the medians barely
change (about 0.031 and 0.026 L/h). The simulated cohort is not split by
response.

```{r fig5, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
cl_compare <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0, last_start + tau)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(when = ifelse(time == 0, "CL at baseline", "CL after 26 weeks"))
cl_compare$when <- factor(cl_compare$when, levels = c("CL at baseline", "CL after 26 weeks"))

ggplot(cl_compare, aes(arm, cl, fill = when)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey60", "white")) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "CL (L/h)", fill = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Wilkins 2019 (responders and non-responders pooled)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

cl_compare |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, when) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_cl = stats::median(cl), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = when, values_from = median_cl) |>
  dplyr::rename("Tumor type" = arm) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "Simulated median clearance (L/h).")
```

# Typical-value checks

The paper states the typical numbers for the time effect: CL falls by at
most 32.1% in mMCC (0.0308 to 0.0209 L/h) and by at most 24.7% in SCCHN
(0.0308 to 0.0232 L/h). The packaged model must give these. Below, a
typical patient at the covariate medians is solved without random
effects, and the solved CL is checked against Eq. 1.

```{r typical}
typ_cov <- data.frame(
  WT = 71, AGE = 63, ALB = 39, CRCL = 85.9, TUMSZ = 60, CRP = 10.7,
  PLT = 247, AST = 22, SEXF = 0, RACE_BLACK = 0, ADA_POS = 0,
  CONMED_OPIOID = 1, PRIOR_BIO = 0
)
typ_arms <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3, arm = c("Urothelial carcinoma", "SCCHN", "mMCC"),
  TUMTP_SCCHN = c(0, 1, 0), TUMTP_MCC = c(0, 0, 1)
)
t_typ <- c(0, 24 * c(1, 28, 68.4, 131, 182, 365, 3650))
ev_typ <- merge(typ_arms, typ_cov) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = t_typ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(merge(typ_arms, typ_cov), time = 0, amt = 710, dur = 1, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  ev_typ
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_typ, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")

# Eq. 1 written out independently from Table 2
eq1 <- function(t_day, imax, t50, g) 0.0308 * exp(imax * t_day^g / (t50^g + t_day^g))
typ$cl_eq1 <- with(typ, ifelse(
  arm == "mMCC", eq1(time / 24, -0.387, 131, 1.68),
  ifelse(arm == "SCCHN", eq1(time / 24, -0.284, 68.4, 0.73), eq1(time / 24, 0, 68.4, 2.91))
))
stopifnot(all(abs(typ$cl / typ$cl_eq1 - 1) < 1e-6))

# Maximal decreases printed in the Results (32.1% and 24.7%)
ini_df <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$iniDf
imax_mcc <- ini_df$est[ini_df$name == "cl_time_max_mcc"]
imax_scchn <- ini_df$est[ini_df$name == "cl_time_max_scchn"]
max_drop <- c(mMCC = 1 - exp(imax_mcc), SCCHN = 1 - exp(imax_scchn))
stopifnot(
  abs(max_drop[["mMCC"]] - 0.321) < 0.0005,
  abs(max_drop[["SCCHN"]] - 0.247) < 0.0005,
  abs(0.0308 * exp(imax_mcc) - 0.0209) < 0.00005,
  abs(0.0308 * exp(imax_scchn) - 0.0232) < 0.00005
)

# The 10-year typical mMCC CL is at its asymptote (0.0209 L/h)
cl_mcc_10y <- typ$cl[typ$arm == "mMCC" & typ$time == max(t_typ)]
stopifnot(abs(cl_mcc_10y - 0.0209) < 0.0001)

typ |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(day = time / 24, cl_rel = cl / 0.0308) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, day, cl, cl_rel) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = day, names_from = arm, values_from = cl_rel) |>
  dplyr::rename("Day" = day) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical CL(t) / CL(0) by tumor type.")
```

The typical terminal half-life at baseline follows from the
two-compartment micro-constants. The paper reports a geometric mean of the
individual (empirical Bayes) half-lives of 4.5 days at baseline. After
26 weeks of dosing it reports 6.8 days in mMCC and 5.7 days in SCCHN,
with no change in the other tumor types.

```{r typical-thalf}
terminal_thalf_day <- function(cl, vc, q, vp) {
  k10 <- cl / vc
  k12 <- q / vc
  k21 <- q / vp
  a <- k10 + k12 + k21
  lz <- (a - sqrt(a^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  log(2) / lz / 24
}
thalf_typ <- typ |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(24, 182 * 24)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(thalf = terminal_thalf_day(cl, vc, q, vp))
thalf_base <- thalf_typ$thalf[thalf_typ$arm == "Urothelial carcinoma" & thalf_typ$time == 24]
stopifnot(abs(thalf_base / 4.5 - 1) < 0.1)

thalf_typ |>
  dplyr::mutate(day = time / 24) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, day, cl, thalf) |>
  dplyr::rename("Tumor type" = arm, "Day" = day, "CL (L/h)" = cl, "Terminal t1/2 (day)" = thalf) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "Typical terminal half-life at day 1 and after 26 weeks.")
```

The typical baseline half-life (`r round(thalf_base, 2)` days) is 5% below
the published geometric mean of the individual estimates. The 26-week
typical values are lower than the published geometric means (6.8 and
5.7 days). Those are averages of empirical Bayes estimates in the treated
patients, which include the random effect on Imax and selective follow-up
of patients who stayed on treatment. They are not the typical-value
quantity computed here.

# PKNCA validation

NCA over the first dosing interval and over the last one, weeks 24-26.

```{r pknca}
nca_window <- function(d, start, label) {
  d |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time >= start, time <= start + tau) |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = time - start, treatment = paste(arm, label, sep = ", "))
}
conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_window(sim, 0, "first dose"),
  nca_window(sim, last_start, "weeks 24-26")
) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc)

dose_nca <- cohort |>
  dplyr::select(id, arm, WT) |>
  tidyr::crossing(label = c("first dose", "weeks 24-26")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste(arm, label, sep = ", "), time = 0, amt = 10 * WT) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = tau,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)

summary(nca_res) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated NCA by tumor type and dosing interval (10 mg/kg every 2 weeks).")
```

The paper's half-life values are geometric means of individual estimates
(Results). Below they are set against the median simulated NCA half-life
for the same tumor type and interval.

```{r nca-compare}
simulated_hl <- nca_df |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life") |>
  dplyr::mutate(PPORRES = PPORRES / 24) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

published <- data.frame(
  treatment = c(
    "Urothelial carcinoma, first dose", "SCCHN, first dose", "mMCC, first dose",
    "Urothelial carcinoma, weeks 24-26", "SCCHN, weeks 24-26", "mMCC, weeks 24-26"
  ),
  half.life = c(4.5, 4.5, 4.5, 4.5, 5.7, 6.8)
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = simulated_hl,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "day"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Tumor type and interval" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Terminal half-life: simulated median versus published geometric mean.",
    "* differs by more than 20%."
  ))

hl_med <- simulated_hl |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(hl = stats::median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
hl_first <- hl_med$hl[grepl("first dose", hl_med$treatment)]
stopifnot(all(abs(hl_first / 4.5 - 1) < 0.25))

# The time effect lengthens the half-life in mMCC and SCCHN but not in UC.
# Typical-value ratios are 1.26 (mMCC) and 1.18 (SCCHN); the thresholds leave
# room for cohort-to-cohort noise in the medians.
hl_ratio <- function(arm) {
  hl_med$hl[hl_med$treatment == paste(arm, "weeks 24-26", sep = ", ")] /
    hl_med$hl[hl_med$treatment == paste(arm, "first dose", sep = ", ")]
}
stopifnot(
  hl_ratio("mMCC") > 1.1,
  hl_ratio("SCCHN") > 1.03,
  abs(hl_ratio("Urothelial carcinoma") - 1) < 0.1
)
```

The simulated median half-lives are within about 10% of the published
geometric means at baseline and in SCCHN after 26 weeks. In mMCC after
26 weeks the simulated median is about 12% below the published 6.8 days,
consistent with the typical-value comparison above.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Placement of the V2 covariances.** Table 2 lists the IIV terms in
  NONMEM output order: omega2 CL, cov(CL,V1), omega2 V1, 0.0633, -0.014,
  omega2 V2. It labels the fourth row "cov(V1,V2)" and the fifth
  "cov(CL,V2)". The published control stream (Data S1) has
  `$OMEGA BLOCK(3)` with row 3 = `0.0625345 -0.0140066 0.853445`, so its
  initial values put about 0.063 at cov(ETA1, ETA3), which is cov(CL,V2),
  and -0.014 at cov(ETA2, ETA3), which is cov(V1,V2). The Table 2 labels
  are also visibly garbled: all three covariance rows carry the subscript
  "CL,V1". The packaged model follows the control stream, so
  cov(CL,V2) = 0.0633 and cov(V1,V2) = -0.014. The Discussion's remark
  that the CL-V2 covariance was imprecise follows the Table 2 labels.
  Both placements give a positive-definite matrix.
- **Final estimates.** Data S1 carries the initial estimates of the final
  run (for example, gamma for SCCHN 0.96 and Imax SCCHN -0.266). The
  model uses the final estimates of Table 2 (0.73 and -0.284), which
  match the Results text.
- **T50 for SCCHN.** Table 2 has no SCCHN-specific T50. In Data S1 the
  SCCHN branch overrides only Imax and gamma, so SCCHN uses the shared
  T50 of 68.4 days, as the Results text says.
- **Covariate handling.** Data S1 imputes missing covariates (coded
  <= 0) to the population median and caps albumin (61 g/L), eGFR (226),
  tumor size (388 mm), CRP (250 mg/L), platelets (600) and AST
  (105 U/L). The model does the same, so a CRP of exactly 0 is also
  treated as 10.7 mg/L. Age is neither capped nor imputed.
- **Opioid effect orientation.** The published effect applies to
  patients *not* taking opioids (-0.0445). The model therefore uses
  `1 - CONMED_OPIOID`, with patients taking opioids as the reference.
- **ADA.** `ADA_POS` is the time-fixed "ever positive" flag the paper
  used (HAHAEVER). Missing ADA status counts as negative.
- **Race coding.** `RACE_BLACK = 1` corresponds to `RACE = 2` in Data S1.
  All other races and missing race form the reference.
- **Tumor-type indicators.** `TUMTP_SCCHN` and `TUMTP_MCC` correspond to
  `TTYPE = 6` and `TTYPE = 14` in Data S1, matching the code comments
  "head and neck" and "MCC". All other tumor types (both zero) share
  typical Imax = 0, T50 = 68.4 days and gamma = 2.91.
- **Parameter scale for Imax.** Imax is kept on its natural scale
  (`cl_time_max`, not log-transformed) because it is zero or negative and
  carries an additive random effect. The convention checker's "should be
  log-transformed" warning for this parameter is expected.
- **Time.** The model time unit is hours (CL and Q in L/h), and the time
  effect uses days after the first dose (`t / 24`). The first dose must
  be at time 0.
- **Infusion duration.** The paper does not state it; the simulations
  use the labelled 1-hour infusion.
- **Virtual cohort.** Covariate distributions are approximations built
  from the Table 1 medians and ranges, drawn independently. Responder
  status (Figures 4 and 5) is not modelled.
- **Errata.** No erratum or correction for this article was found in
  Europe PMC (checked 2026-11-25).
